title: Erasure of entanglement-locked energy in multi-cell quantum batteries through decoherence
authors: Haniyeh Hajizade, Vahid Ameri, Alidad Askari
abstract: Charging a quantum battery through a pumped charger can lock a substantial part of its stored energy inside the bipartite correlations that grow between the constituent cells, and this \emph{correlation ergotropy}, being the energy that no local single-cell operation can reach and that only collective operations can recover, is the object of the present study. Following the charging trajectory of two coupled three-level cells, we find that the correlation ergotropy closely tracks the logarithmic negativity, which shows that the locked energy is carried by genuine bipartite entanglement rather than by coherent collective dynamics alone, and that an equal-strength coherent non-entangling drive produces no such locking at all. For a pure two-cell battery we establish an exact, basis-independent closed form in which the locked energy depends only on the sorted eigenvalues of the reduced cell and the cell energy levels, revealing that the locked fraction rises from zero at the separable corners of the Schmidt simplex to unity at the symmetric maximally entangled state and remains invariant under local unitaries. Decoherence and dephasing, which destroy the correlations, do \emph{not} release this energy but erase it, so extraction must be collective and must take place while the correlations persist, while cold damping leaves the effect intact and thermal occupation suppresses it. These results give a resource-theoretic reading of correlations in quantum batteries, sharpen the line between genuine entanglement and coherent collective dynamics, and point to experimentally accessible conditions for correlated-charge and collective-extraction protocols.
summary: This paper quantifies the 'correlation ergotropy' in quantum batteries, demonstrating that a significant portion of stored energy is locked in genuine bipartite entanglement, inaccessible by local operations. The authors show this locked energy tracks entanglement measures and that decoherence erases this resource rather than releasing it. This provides a resource-theoretic framework for understanding collective energy extraction in quantum devices.
main_problem: The study investigates the 'correlation ergotropy'—energy locked in bipartite correlations within a quantum battery that cannot be accessed by local operations.
main_result: The locked energy is shown to track the logarithmic negativity, confirming that genuine bipartite entanglement, rather than just coherent dynamics, is the resource responsible for this energy storage.
method: The authors use the Lindblad master equation to model open-system dynamics and define the correlation ergotropy as the difference between global and local extractable work.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum battery composed of coupled three-level atoms (qutrits) charged by a pumped charger. The analysis compares charging dynamics under an entangling charger versus a non-entangling coherent drive.
key_observables: Correlation Ergotropy ($W_{corr}$), Logarithmic Negativity ($N$), Global Ergotropy ($W_g$), and Local Ergotropy ($W_l$).
important_parameters: Low temperature regime, coupling strength ($\lambda$), and the presence/absence of decoherence/dephasing.
main_assumptions: The analysis is most rigorous for pure two-cell states, and the collective advantage is confirmed in the low-temperature limit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate that $W_{corr}$ tracks $N$ along the charging path, that $W_l=0$ when $W_{corr}>0$, and that decoherence erases the locked energy rather than releasing it.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the definition of correlation ergotropy, compares its behavior under entangled vs. coherent driving, derives an analytical form for pure states, and tests the robustness of the locked energy against decoherence.
why_interesting: This work provides a resource-theoretic quantification of entanglement in energy storage, directly linking quantum correlation measures (like entanglement) to measurable thermodynamic quantities (extractable work) in systems relevant to AMO physics (e.g., trapped ions, Rydberg atoms).

Charging trajectory of two qutrit cells with a quan- tum (entangling) charger (Ω= 0.7ω, λ = 0.4ω): stored en- ergy E, global ergotropy Wg, local ergotropy Wl, correlation ergotropy Wcorr = Wg −Wl, and logarithmic negativity N. At the correlation peak Wl = 0 while Wg > 0, and Wcorr tracks N.

FIG. 2. Correlation ergotropy Wcorr versus logarithmic nega- tivity N along the charging trajectory of two qutrit cells. The near-linear relation (dashed line, Pearson rP = 0.89, Spear- man rS = 0.91) confirms that the locked energy is carried by genuine bipartite entanglement.

FIG. 4. Extractable fraction at matched stored energy E for the quantum (entangling) charger and the coherent (non- entangling) drive. The coherent drive extracts all of its stored energy locally (Wg = Wl = E), while the entangled charger leaves Wl = 0 and reaches at most Wg/E ≃47% over the range shown. Entanglement transforms locally accessible en- ergy into correlation ergotropy rather than increasing it.
